elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 13 is retained unchanged: "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)" — Sparkling owns nothing, including the Schedule "D" Modifications built for it.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained: "No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement." No assignment operation was proposed.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 13 (untouched) confirms Garman owns all IP in the Work and related materials, logos and names.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 2: "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and non-exclusive licence to use, modify and sublicense" the Software and Documentation (which is Garman IP).

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 2 expressly states the licence is "irrevocable".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 2 states "royalty-free", and the additional-fee-for-other-locations sentence is removed.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: No operative sentence anywhere states that Sparkling owns or retains all rights in its data; the only new data language limits Garman's use, which is not an affirmative ownership/retention statement.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: New clause: "Garman's use of Sparkling's data is limited to processing it solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists or is created; Section 13 allocates ownership solely to Garman and the new grant is a licence only.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 13 retained untouched: "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 2 grants "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and non-exclusive licence" to the Software and Documentation.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "irrevocable" appears expressly in the rendered Section 2 grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" is added and the conflicting "Authorized Locations"/"at each AS400" limits and the additional-fee sentence are deleted, so no retained sentence contradicts the geographic scope.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" is stated and the sentence conditioning use at other locations on "payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule" is removed.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "licence to use, modify and sublicense for Sparkling's business: (i) the Software ...; and (ii) the Documentation."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Section 2 grants the right to "sublicense for Sparkling's business", and Section 3(c) is conformed: "except as permitted under Section 2 or as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing", so no retained prohibition contradicts it.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: New clause (c): "Garman's use of Sparkling's data is limited to processing it solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: Section 2 now reads perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free with express use, modify and sublicense rights for Sparkling's business; Section 3(c) is conformed so permitted sublicensing is not separately barred; and a new clause caps Garman's use of Sparkling's data at processing solely to provide the services. Garman's Section 13 ownership of its own software and know-how is left intact, satisfying the generic-tools element.

The preferred level is correctly not claimed: ownership of the Work (including the Schedule "D" Modifications) stays with Garman, there is no assignment to Sparkling, and no sentence states that Sparkling retains all rights in its data. Flagging this as a deviation targeted at the fallback is the right call.

Minimality holds. Every deletion in Section 2 is load-bearing: "non-transferable" contradicts the sublicense element; "operating at Authorized Locations" and "at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations" contradict worldwide (and the AS400 fragment would be ambiguous if left orphaned); and the additional-fee sentence directly contradicts royalty-free/worldwide, so retaining it would have created a contradictory retained sentence. No survival tail, expense language or extra procedure was added.

Intent is preserved: the Fee Schedule, the Authorized Locations definition (still used in the Future Installations clause) and the termination mechanics survive, and the comment correctly defers the term/termination interaction to the termination rule rather than duplicating it here.

Recommended (non-blocking) tightening: Section 13 distinguishes "the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)" from "the Software", so consider adding "(including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)" to the Section 2 subject matter. Without it, a counterparty could argue the upgraded licence reaches only the base Software and Documentation and not the custom Schedule "D" Modifications that the rationale identifies as our deliverable.

Two drafting checks before sending: confirm the new data clause lettered "(c)" does not collide with an existing subsection in the Future Installations/Conversions section (renumber if it does), and consider using the agreement's capitalised services/Support term instead of lower-case "services under this Agreement" so the limitation cannot be read narrowly.
